correctness.rationale: A full all-triangle proof uses ordered nodal gaps and a convex quadratic on [0,1]^2; two exact completing-square identities give the metric-angle upper bound; explicit one-sided and bounded clipping values attain the upper bound at every obtuse vertex, and values inside clip interval attain one on nonobtuse triangles. The constant-diffusion affine coordinate transformation is exact. The rational-stiffness 120-degree counterexample and independent NumPy checker corroborate the equations. Limits: no global mesh sharpness beyond the summable upper bound.

evidence: Prior 1D nodal H1 contraction holds because a mesh interval carries a single nodal difference, whereas a triangle carries a sum of two vectors whose angle can be obtuse.

Prior pointwise cutoff H1 energy decrease follows from the chain rule; the explicit three-node example has energy ratio 4/3 after nodal reinterpolation, so the two operators are mathematically inequivalent.
Delaunay-type maximum-principle mesh criteria do not specify an optimal amplification magnitude for the stated elementwise operator.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The older positive contraction statements do not imply the proposed theorem: one is restricted to 1D P1 intervals, the other uses pointwise spatial clipping. Conversely the new theorem reduces to the nonexpansive statement for nonobtuse transformed triangles and refines it to exact amplification in the obtuse case; it neither contradicts nor subsumes general maximum-principle error estimates. Specialized prior exact-angle results remain a documented risk.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The precise local operator is R_T(P(x)), where R_T is barycentric P1 reinterpolation of clipped nodal values. The spatial pointwise map P(R_T(x)) is generally piecewise affine only on a refined cut submesh and has a different gradient and energy. The 1D estimate lacks the interaction of two nonorthogonal gradients. Neither equivalent-looking assertion implies the obtuse-angle amplification factor.

value.rationale: Elementwise nodal cutoff is a standard maximum-bound-preserving postprocessor for numerical PDEs. Its impact on the gradient-energy functional matters for simultaneous energy stability; the exact metric-angle amplification supplies a natural mesh-aware diagnostic, identifies an if-and-only-if elementwise energy-safe geometry for the specified clip, and quantifies deterioration for nearly degenerate obtuse cells. The theorem stands without claiming full-scheme performance or convergence.
